content: The text provided appears to be a long list of clinical trials and studies related to antiretroviral therapies for HIV treatment. 1. A randomized study compared a nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI)-sparing regimen of raltegravir (RAL) combined with lopinavir/ritonavir (LPV/r) versus efavirenz/tenofovir disoproxil fumarate/emtricitabine (EFV/TDF/FTC) in antiretroviral-naive patients. (De Jesus et al., 2011) 2. A clinical trial evaluated abacavir versus zidovudine, each combined with lamivudine and efavirenz, for the treatment of antiretroviral-naive HIV-infected adults. (Vibhagool et al., 2004) 3. A 48-week open-label equivalence trial compared triple nucleoside treatment with abacavir plus a lamivudine/zidovudine combination tablet to indinavir combined with the same lamivudine/zidovudine combination in antiretroviral-naive adults. (Staszewski et al., 2001) 4. A randomized trial assessed the efficacy of a triple nucleoside combination of zidovudine/lamivudine/abacavir versus zidovudine/lamivudine/nelfinavir as first-line therapy in HIV-1-infected adults. (Matheron et al., 2003) 5. A study compared the metabolic and body habitus effects of nevirapine versus nelfinavir in antiretroviral-naive HIV-infected patients. (Fisac et al., 2003) 6. A randomized clinical trial evaluated the safety and efficacy of nelfinavir or nevirapine combined with zidovudine/lamivudine in HIV-infected naive patients. (Podzamczer et al., 2002) 7. The NRTI Sparing Trial (CTN 177) investigated the antiviral and metabolic effects of nevirapine (NVP) plus lopinavir/ritonavir (LPV/r) versus zidovudine/lamivudine (AZT/3TC) plus NVP or AZT/3TC plus LPV/r in antiretroviral-naive HIV-infected patients. (Harris et al., 2009) 8. A study reported a high rate of early virological failure with the once-daily tenofovir/lamivudine/nevirapine combination in naive HIV-1-infected patients. (Rey et al., 2009) 9. A phase 3 randomized, double-blind, active-controlled trial compared rilpivirine versus efavirenz, both combined with tenofovir and emtricitabine, in treatment-naive adults with HIV-1 infection. (Landman et al., 2011) 10. The ENCORE 1 study demonstrated the efficacy of a reduced 400 mg dose of efavirenz compared to the standard 600 mg dose in HIV-infected, antiretroviral-naive adults. (Amin et al., 2014) 11. A randomized multicenter trial in Japanese patients with HIV-1 infection compared abacavir/lamivudine versus tenofovir/emtricitabine, both combined with atazanavir/ritonavir. (Nishijima et al., 2013) 12. The FLAMINGO study compared once-daily dolutegravir versus darunavir plus ritonavir in antiretroviral-naive adults with HIV-1 infection, reporting 48-week and 96-week results. (Clotet et al., 2014) 13. The GEMINI study evaluated the non-inferiority of saquinavir/ritonavir versus lopinavir/ritonavir as initial HIV-1 therapy in adults. (Walmsley et al., 2009) 14. A randomized, double-blind trial compared single-tablet regimens of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF versus efavirenz/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF for initial HIV-1 treatment, with analyses at weeks 96 and 144. (Zolopa et al., 2014) 15. The STARTMRK trial assessed long-term treatment with raltegravir or efavirenz combined with tenofovir/emtricitabine in treatment-naive HIV-1-infected patients. (De Jesus et al., 2012) 16. The SPRING-2 study compared once-daily dolutegravir versus twice-daily raltegravir in antiretroviral-naive adults with HIV-1 infection, reporting 48-week and 96-week results. (Raffi et al., 2013) 17. The SAILING study evaluated the safety and efficacy of dolutegravir in combination therapy for antiretroviral-naive adults with HIV. (Min et al., 2013) 18. The KLEAN study compared fosamprenavir-ritonavir versus lopinavir-ritonavir, each combined with abacavir-lamivudine, for initial HIV treatment over 48 weeks. (Eron et al., 2006) 19. The PROGRESS study examined the non-inferiority, safety, and tolerability of lopinavir/ritonavir combined with raltegravir versus lopinavir/ritonavir combined with tenofovir/emtricitabine in antiretroviral-naive subjects. (Reynes et al., 2011) 20. The RADAR study reported similar safety and antiviral efficacy of raltegravir combined with boosted darunavir compared to tenofovir/emtricitabine combined with boosted darunavir in antiretroviral-naive patients. (Bedimo et al., 2011) 21. The SEARCH 003 study evaluated the safety and efficacy of switching from stavudine to zidovudine at 24 weeks compared to zidovudine or tenofovir DF, when given with lamivudine and nevirapine. (Phanuphak et al., 2012) 22. The SENC trial compared efavirenz versus nevirapine in a randomized, open-label study in HIV-infected naive individuals. (Nunez et al., 2002) 23. The OzCombo study compared three highly active antiretroviral therapy regimens, including two nucleoside analogues and indinavir, for previously untreated HIV-1 infection. (Carr et al., 2000) 24. A study assessed the impact of lamivudine on HIV and hepatitis B virus-related outcomes in HIV/hepatitis B co-infected individuals in a randomized clinical trial of antiretroviral therapy in southern Africa. (French et al., 2011) 25. The START I study compared stavudine plus lamivudine versus zidovudine plus lamivudine in combination with indinavir in antiretroviral-naive individuals with HIV infection. (Squires et al., 2004) 26. The STAR study demonstrated that a single-tablet regimen of rilpivirine/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF maintained non-inferiority to efavirenz/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF and had minimal impact on fasting lipids in ART-naive adults. (Cohen et al., 2013) 27. A randomized comparison of integrase inhibitors with TDF/FTC was conducted to evaluate renal markers. (Bracchi et al., 2017) 28. The NEAT 001/ANRS 143 trial compared ritonavir-boosted darunavir combined with raltegravir versus tenofovir-emtricitabine in antiretroviral-naive adults with HIV-1 infection, reporting 96-week results. (Raffi et al., 2014) 29. The NORA trial compared the safety and efficacy of nevirapine versus abacavir in combination with zidovudine/lamivudine as first-line antiretroviral therapy in Ugandan adults with low CD4 cell counts. (Munderi et al., 2008) 30. A study evaluated the metabolic effects of darunavir/ritonavir versus atazanavir/ritonavir in treatment-naive HIV-1-infected subjects over 48 weeks. (Torti et al.
